questions.excerpt:
Foreword The present trend of rapidly increased population of our county and the accent on
            suburban shopping has resulted in a major problem for our county road system. Developments
            and subdivisions have sprung up almost overnight and with them the inevitable gas
            stations, hopping centers, amusement areas and other myriad interests that go along
            with a growing community. The inevitable problems thereby generated include the necessity
            of caring for increased traffic, drainage, safety of pedestrians and motorists, zoning,
            building ordinances, etc. These problems have been the subject of a great deal of
            study by municipal officials, planning boards and others, and it is their concern
            for the future that prompted the enactment into Law, effective April 14, 1958, of
            the new Section 239-k of the General Municipal Law (Chapter 740 of the Laws of 1958)
            that appears on the following pages. The authorizing legislation states that the county's
            regulations shall be in consideration of: "the prospective character of the development
            (or building), the traffic which it will generate, the effect of said traffic upon
            existing County Roads … the design and frequency of access, the effect, … upon drainage
            as related to the county drainage system, and the extent to which such development
            may impair the safety and traffic-carrying capacity of the county roads affected."
            These rules and regulations are issued pursuant to the above-cited legislation and
            are designed to furnish information and promulgate standards governing the issuance
            of approvals for building construction affecting the county road system. Extract from "County Official Map Act", Chapter 740, Laws of 1958 (Sections 239-g
            to 239-k, inclusive, Article 12-B, General Municipal Law) Sec. 239-k.…
